speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry will review the current migrant domestic worker hiring policies and rules to allow for more diverse care arrangements of the elderly, such as those in the private co-living care format; and (b) what are the Ministry's concerns and constraints preventing more flexibility in such employment rules and what are the statistics or data that give rise to these concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The well-being of MDWs and the conditions of their engagement are important priorities for the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Government recognises the diverse needs of the elderly and their caregivers and has introduced a wide range of eldercare services to support households.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: These include home personal and nursing care, day care and community rehabilitation services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Ministry of National Development (MND), Ministry of Health (MOH) and Housing and Development Board (HDB) are also piloting assisted living in the Community Care Apartments, which integrates senior-friendly design features with services that can be scaled according to the care needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: There are also a number of private assisted living models for seniors to age in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM has been and will continue to work closely with MOH and industry partners to explore new and holistic caregiving models to better support eldercare needs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Despite that, is MOM open to looking at new regulatory frameworks and provisions for different kinds of employment models such that the gap that the residents and citizens currently face in elderly care options can be plugged in a way that ensures that business costs, cost to consumers and all that are made accessible and viable?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We recognise that there are evolving needs and there are opportunities for us to work with private partners to develop new models.
